Requested service/CPT: Lower back disc surgery / decompression, CPT 63030
Appeal must be received by: 2027-02-18

To the Appeals and Grievances Department:

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 63030 (lumbar laminotomy/discectomy with nerve root decompression), as set out in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-22, reference number POC-BDD7B46260-11524. The stated reason for denial was that "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure."

I am requesting that Tufts Health Plan reverse this determination and approve the requested surgery, performed by Dr. Duval, MD (orthopedic surgery). Below I address the stated reason for denial and map my clinical record to the applicable medical-necessity criteria.

Applicable medical-necessity criteria

Tufts Health Plan's Medical Specialty Solutions program for musculoskeletal/spine surgery is administered by National Imaging Associates, Inc. (NIA), a subsidiary of Evolent. NIA/Evolent's published clinical guideline for this procedure category, "Evolent Clinical Guideline 1766 for Lumbar Spine Surgery," lists CPT 63030 under "Lumbar Microdiscectomy" and states the surgical indications as follows (quoted directly from the guideline text I obtained):

"When ALL of the following are present:
o Primary radicular symptoms noted upon clinical exam that significantly hinders daily activities
o Failure of conservative treatment* for a minimum of six (6) weeks within the last six (6) months
NOTE - Failure of conservative treatment is defined as one of the following:
• Lack of meaningful improvement after a full course of treatment; OR
• Progression or worsening of symptoms during treatment; OR
• Documentation of a medical reason the member is unable to participate in treatment
o Imaging studies showing evidence of inter-vertebral disc herniation that correlate exactly with the individual's symptoms/signs"

I could not independently confirm, from a document bearing Tufts Health Plan's own name, that this exact edition of the guideline is the one applied to my case. I am relying on it because Tufts Health Plan's published provider Quick Reference Guide confirms that Tufts contracts with NIA/Evolent to manage prior authorization for inpatient and outpatient musculoskeletal surgeries, including elective spine surgery. If a different or more specific criteria set was actually used to deny my request, I ask that Tufts Health Plan identify that document by name, number, and effective date, and provide me a copy, as required for a full and fair review.

How my clinical record meets each criterion

1. "Primary radicular symptoms noted upon clinical exam that significantly hinders daily activities"
My record documents 18 months of progressive low back pain, unrelieved by rest, with radicular pain extending into my right calf. I am unable to stand for more than 10 minutes at a time. Exam findings include positive provocative testing on the affected (right) side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level. This directly supports radicular symptoms that significantly hinder daily activities.

2. "Failure of conservative treatment* for a minimum of six (6) weeks within the last six (6) months"
I completed a supervised physical therapy program (core stabilization and lumbar flexibility), 20 visits over 10 weeks, from 2026-05-11 to 2026-07-20, as documented in my physical therapy discharge note — well in excess of the six-week minimum. I also used NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief, and received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-23 that provided only 4 weeks of partial relief before symptoms returned. Under the guideline's own definition, this constitutes "[l]ack of meaningful improvement after a full course of treatment," satisfying the failure-of-conservative-treatment element.

3. "Imaging studies showing evidence of inter-vertebral disc herniation that correlate exactly with the individual's symptoms/signs"
MRI of the lumbar spine dated 2026-06-15 shows an L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing right L5 nerve root. This finding correlates exactly, level for level and side for side, with my clinical presentation: right-sided radicular pain into the calf (an L5 distribution), positive provocative testing on the right, and a neurologic deficit corresponding to this same imaged level.

There is no active infection, no untreated substance use, and I am a non-smoker with a BMI of 29 — none of which raise any relative contraindication under the portions of the guideline addressing risk factors that I was able to review.

Requested action

Based on the above, my clinical record satisfies each element required under the "Lumbar Discectomy/Microdiscectomy" surgical indications in the guideline identified above. I ask that Tufts Health Plan:

1. Reverse the denial of CPT 63030 and issue a prior authorization approval; or
2. If the denial is upheld, identify by name, number, and effective date the specific medical policy or clinical criteria actually relied upon (if different from the guideline discussed above), explain in writing which specific criterion within that document my submitted imaging and records failed to meet, and provide me a copy of that document; and
3. Arrange, at my request, a peer-to-peer conversation between Dr. Duval and the reviewing physician, and ensure that the reviewer on this appeal is a clinical peer in the same or similar specialty who was not involved in the original denial.

Enclosed with this appeal are copies of: the MRI report dated 2026-06-15; the physical therapy discharge note (2026-05-11 to 2026-07-20); records of NSAID use and the 2026-05-23 corticosteroid injection; and clinic notes documenting exam findings and functional limitations. Please contact me or my attending surgeon, Dr. Duval, if any additional information is needed.

I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-02-18, and I am submitting it well in advance of that deadline. Please send written acknowledgment of receipt of this appeal, including the name, address, and telephone number of the person coordinating the review, as provided for under Tufts Health Plan's appeals procedure.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Sincerely,

Skyler Foster
